notes: Same standards as the previous sweep's macro-dsl grade files and the 2026-10-21-check grade file: the import/alias rule is graded on what __using__ injects and whether the effects of use sit in an admonition at the top of @moduledoc; a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, validation in the macro body (outside quote) does not; `if not ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule; a one-line three-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens; generated routes/0 and match/1 without @doc are not counted, as in those files.

Changed rule, graded against the text at db91c23 (idiomatic-elixir/references/library-design.md, line 61): Add specs, and hide technical functions from the docs. Violating runs out of five, per decisive sentence or clause. "Give every public function a `@spec`, including functions marked `@doc false`": 0 of 5 (every @doc false function, __route__/3, __define__/3, __match__/2 or TinyRouter.match/2, has a @spec). "and functions a macro defines in the caller's module, where the `@spec` goes inside the `quote`, directly above the `def`": 0 of 5 (all five put a @spec directly above the generated def routes and def match inside the __before_compile__ quote). "A function that implements a `@callback` under `@impl` needs none; the callback carries the types.": decided no verdict, 0 of 5 runs used @callback or @impl. "Mark functions that are public only for technical reasons, such as functions called from macro-generated code, with `@doc false`." (unchanged): 0 of 5. At 93873be the previous sweep had 3 of 5 runs violating this rule (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1), and opus-1 was clean only through the @callback/@impl reading.

macros.md also changed since 93873be, but only inside the Keep `quote` blocks small example (a @spec line above def __define__); the rule's prose is unchanged, so it and the other five listed rules are graded to the previous standard.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects (one per run, the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, so xref line numbers match the run file, with real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex). haiku-1 expands the handler with Macro.expand and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile), the previous sweep's route to the violation. haiku-2 passes the alias unexpanded into a function call that runs in the router's module body and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile), the check batch's route. opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use Macro.expand_literals with a function set in the env and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime).

Bad-declaration checks: each run's file loaded, then one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and another declaring get "/", "not a module" compiled with Code.compile_string. All ten fail while the router compiles: opus-1 and haiku-2 with ArgumentError from the function get's quote calls; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 with CompileError raised while get expands. Messages below omit the nofile:3: location prefix.

Format: opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2 pass mix format --check-formatted. haiku-2 (lines 115-116) and sonnet-1 (lines 134-135) fail it only because they wrote get "/", MyApp.PageHandler without parentheses in the example router, which result.json records as format_ok false. All five compile without warnings with elixir and with mix compile.

Reads: all five read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing the file. opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 used Read calls and read each reference file twice; haiku-2 read both references with one cat in a Bash call. This matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope"; the haiku runs return atom param keys (%{id: "42"}), the others string keys (%{"id" => "42"}).
